newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cheung Kong sees higher rental income.
newsitem.headline: Cheung Kong sees higher rental income.

text.p: Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd said it should generate considerable cash income from the sale of several residential projects in 1997 while rental income from Hong Kong and China would increase greatly over coming years.

"The group expects to release several residential projects for sale in 1997, including The Green Wood at Laguna Verde and Maywood Court at Kingswood Villas. These will bring in considerable cash income to the group," Cheung Kong said in a statement on Wednesday.
The Hong Kong property developer said its projects were progressing as scheduled and some non-residential properties would be kept for rental to strengthen recurrent income.
"It is anticipated that in the next few years, rental income from both Hong Kong and mainland China will increase greatly," it added.
Cheung Kong said its investments on the mainland were making "good progress".
"In particular, the hotels and certain rental properties have been in operation for several years and have made a profit contribution in 1996," it said.

Cheung Kong earlier reported a 23.7 percent rise in 1996 net profit to HK$13.77 billion, including a HK$1.51 billion exceptional gain from the placement and new issue of shares in Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd.
